div.ab: Habeat quilibet primariorum quolibet anno de nostra warda, quam [uu]ichin Angli appellant, duos equos, unum cum sella, alterum sine sella, unum gladium, V lanceas, unum cuspidem, unum scutum et ducentos solidos argenti.

div.ab: Let each of the chief men have each year from our ward [store], which the English call [uu]ichin [?], two horses, one with a saddle, the other without a saddle, one sword, five lances, one spear, one shield and two hundred shillings of silver.

wice (acc. wican) Ags., wiken Mengl.: Dienstamt (für e der Endung schreiben Mittelengländer oft i); noch näher stehen der Bedeutung Wirthschaftshaltung die Ableitungen wicnere (dispensator), wicnung (procuratio) Die Gehältertabelle bald nach 1135 nennt sich Constitutio domus regis de procurationibus; ed. Hall Red book of Exchequer 807

Anglo-Saxon wice (acc. wican), Middle English wiken: office of service (Middle English writers often write i for the e of the ending); closer still to the meaning 'housekeeping' are the derivatives wicnere (dispensator), wicnung (procuratio). The table of salaries from soon after 1135 is entitled Constitutio domus regis de procurationibus; ed. Hall, Red book of Exchequer 807.

fürs 13. Jh. steht das Gehalt der zwei Forstmeister fest: für den Süden £ 100, für den Norden 100 Mark; Turner p. xvi. Der Fälscher setzt willkürliche Stücke anderen Zusammenhangs ein, nämlich aus Cnuts Heergewaete

For the 13th century the salary of the two chief foresters is established: £100 for the south, 100 marks for the north; Turner p. xvi. The forger inserts arbitrary items from another context, namely from Cnut's heriot.

That is, 6½ pence a day, which is far too little, for according to the Const. 813 (see note k) even the milites uenatores receive from the royal court 8 d. in die unusquisque.

Die vier Grafschafts-Forstrichter, die Verf. meint, stehen jedenfalls weit tiefer als der oder die zwei Oberrichter des Forsts in ganz England. Der Ritter erhielt unter Heinrich II. 8 Pf. Tagessold; Round Archaeolog. Jl. 59 (1902), 148

The four county forest judges whom the author means rank in any case far below the one or two chief justices of the forest for the whole of England. Under Henry II a knight received 8 pence a day in pay; Round Archaeolog. Jl. 59 (1902), 148
